Core needle biopsy reveals “leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth”—a classic histopathological description of **phyllodes tumor**, specifically suggesting a **cellular phyllodes tumor**, given the emphasis on stromal overgrowth (though definitive classification—benign, borderline, or malignant—requires full histologic assessment including margin status, stromal mitotic activity, and atypia).
